newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen down in line with Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen down in line with Wall Street.

text.p: Thai stocks were expected to fall slightly on Thursday in line with a decline on Wall Street overnight and investor worries that the U.S. might raise interest rates, brokers said

"A fall on Wall Street overnight plus concerns among investors that the U.S. may increase its interest rates in May will be major factors in the SET today. However, the index won't fall much as foreign investors are expected to continue buying," said Thanadech Mahapokai of Book Club Finance.
The SET index fell 2.73 points to 712.63 on 2.7 billion baht turnover on Wednesday.
Brokers said investors were a bit jittery because local interest rates could go up if the U.S. increased its rates.
Foreign investors have been accumulating cheap, fundamental-based stocks for nearly one month.

Brokers said investors had discounted yesterday's announcements by Moody's Investors Service on downgrading the foreign currency ceilings for bonds and bank deposits of Thailand to A3 from A2. It has also cut the senior debt and deposit ratings of five Thai banks to A3 from A2.
